$f(t, z) = ⟨2\cos t, _____, z⟩$

The vector-valued function $f(t, z)$ above parametrizes the elliptic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $x^{2} + y^{2} = 4$. What is the second component of $f$?

$f(t, y) = ⟨2\cos t, y, _____⟩$

The vector-valued function $f(t, y)$ above parametrizes the elliptic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $9x^{2} + 4z^{2} = 36$. What is the third component of $f$?

$$
f(t,z)=⟨\text{_____},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,z)$ above parametrizes the elliptic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as ${x}^{2}+25{y}^{2}=25.$ What is the first component of $f?$
source_solution:
Recall that the ellipse 

$$
{x}^{2}+25{y}^{2}=25\,⟹\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{1}=1
$$

in $xy$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,y⟩=⟨5\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,t\in [0,2\pi ),
$$

since 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{1} & =\frac{(5\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}}{25}+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2} \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t,z) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨5\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in [0,2\pi )$ and $z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $5\operatorname{cos}⁡t.$

source_prompt:
$$
f(t,z)=⟨5\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\text{_____},\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(t,z)$ above parametrizes the elliptic cylinder defined in Cartesian coordinates as $\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}=1.$ What is the second component of $f?$
source_solution:
Recall that the ellipse $\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}=1$ in $xy$-plane has the parametrization

$$
⟨x,y⟩=⟨5\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,t\in [0,2\pi ),
$$

since 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & =\frac{(5\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}}{5}+\frac{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}}{4} \\  & =\frac{25{cos}^{2}⁡t}{25}+\frac{4{sin}^{2}⁡t}{4} \\  & ={cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t,z) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨5\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,z⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in [0,2\pi )$ and $z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the second component of $f$ is $2\operatorname{sin}⁡t.$
